newsitem.title: USA: High consumer debt worries U.S. comptroller Ludwig.
newsitem.headline: High consumer debt worries U.S. comptroller Ludwig.

text.p: U.S. Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig voiced concern on Thursday about the high level of consumer debt and the deteriorating credit quality of consumer loans.
However, Ludwig said the consumer loan problems were not widespread and did not pose a threat to the banking system, which he described as "strong."

"We are concerned about the high levels of debt held by cosumers today," Ludwig said in prepared testimony to the House Banking Committee. "These high levels leave many consumers, and therefore the banks that lend to them, vulnerable to financial shocks."

Ludwig singled out the rapid growth of credit card loans as one area of concern. "(We are) concerned about the recent rise in delinquencies and defaults among credit card loans, although we do not believe there is a widespread or systemic problem," he said.
A survey in May by his office of 82 of the largest national banks found that credit risk had increased in a significant number of areas, particularly credit card loans.
That increased credit risk has prompted many banks to take a more conservative approach to credit card lending, he said.
"We are beginning to see signs that credit card and other banks are responding to the rise in delinquencies and thus are slowing their growth rates for credit card loans," he said.
Ludwig said his office has just completed an updated section on credit cards in its lending handbook and plans to distribute copies in the next several weeks.

It will also issue an advisory letter to banks soon on pre-approved credit card solicitations sent to consumers, alerting the banks to practices that could have an adverse impact on their loan portfolios.

"While we do not believe that consumer credit quality problems have risen to a level where they threaten the soundness of the banking system, we remain concerned about trends in credit quality, particularly given the rise in consumer debt and bankruptcies," Ludwig said at the end of his prepared testimony.
